verification_questions.question: Is there a new deterministic unit test proving that two same-actor edits to the same task with equal (or non-increasing) timestamps converge to the LAST edit's value, and does that test fail against the pre-fix reducer/producer behavior?

Does the fix address the root cause (ordering key too coarse to sequence a single actor's rapid edits) rather than a symptom — i.e. it is NOT merely rewriting e2e spec timestamps or special-casing test code to dodge the gate?

Do the existing CRDT convergence/idempotence/commutativity property tests (task-reducer.property.test.ts, multi-client.property.test.ts) still pass, and was the reducer NOT reverted to a `>=` gate (which would reintroduce inter-author divergence)?
Is the change minimal and scoped to the four mutation event types plus the necessary producer(s)/test/docs, with no unrelated refactors or scope creep?

Does the fix compose cleanly with the forthcoming `updatedByDevice` (MLS clientId) third tie-break level — i.e. it targets the sequential-ordering axis (finer/monotonic timestamp) and does not occupy or alter the concurrent inter-author/inter-device tie-break in a way that would block adding the device level later?
Does the full unit test suite (`make test`) pass with no regressions relative to the recorded baseline counts?

Was docs/task-protocol.md updated to reflect the actual timestamp-resolution/ordering semantics chosen, consistent with the code (including the Task interface field comments and the reducer-semantics section)?

If the fix changes timestamp resolution or wire format, was it verified that task createdAt/updatedAt are never consumed as display dates nor compared against second-granularity values elsewhere (e.g. the kind-30078 bootstrap payload, created_at sort paths), so no consumer breaks?

fix.approach: B - sender-side monotonic timestamp + synchronous stateRef advance
